Treat every agent like a tenant you don't trust yet.

A tenant gets three things.

1

Identity

Every agent is somebody. A verifiable identity the platform issued, not a string the agent claims.

2

Policy

What it may touch, written down, enforced outside the agent. Not a suggestion in a system prompt.

3

No ambient authority

Nothing by default. No cloud credentials in the environment, no open network, no shared filesystem.

Guardrails as an API.

One AgentWorkload in Git. KRO materializes the guardrails. The developer never hand-writes a NetworkPolicy.

The platform team's half.

apiVersion: kro.run/v1alpha1
kind: ResourceGraphDefinition
metadata:
  name: agentworkload
spec:
  schema:
    apiVersion: acme.dev/v1alpha1
    kind: AgentWorkload
    spec:
      agent: string
      isolation: string | default="gvisor"
      network: string | default="default-deny"
      broker: string | default="openshell"
spec:
  resources:
    - id: sandbox
      template:
        kind: Sandbox
        spec: { runtimeClassName: ${schema.spec.isolation} }
    - id: netpol
      template:
        kind: NetworkPolicy
        spec: { policyTypes: [Egress] }
    - id: identity
      template: { kind: ServiceAccount }
    - id: rbac
      template:
        kind: RoleBinding
        subjects: [{ name: ${identity.metadata.name} }]
    - id: quota
      template: { kind: ResourceQuota }

The platform team writes this once. Every agent inherits it.

Illustrative shape. Verify fields against the KRO ResourceGraphDefinition docs for your version.

Two kinds of sandbox.

Kata: hard isolation

Each sandbox is a lightweight virtual machine with its own guest kernel, behind a hardware-virtualized boundary. Even root in the guest cannot reach the host kernel. Strongest boundary. The warm pool hides the startup cost.

gVisor: soft isolation

A userspace kernel that intercepts the application's syscalls. No virtual machine, so it is lighter and faster to start. The app thinks it is talking to Linux.

agent-sandbox picks the runtime per workload via RuntimeClass. This talk's pool runs Kata. The next demo proves the boundary from inside the guest: runtimeClassName: kata

The secure path must be the fast path.

A pre-warmed sandbox pool. Claim one, get it in under a second. Nobody bypasses the sandbox for performance.

Live demo: time the claim

$ time kubectl apply -f claim.yaml

apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: SandboxClaim
metadata:
  name: agent-7
spec:
  warmPoolRef:
    name: agent-pool

Shape per agent-sandbox v1beta1 (warmPoolRef). Check your version's API.

Default deny, explicit allow.

The agent doesn't choose where it goes. The platform decides, per destination, before the packet leaves.

Live demo: two curls

$ curl https://evil.example.com
denied
$ curl https://api.allowed.com
200 OK

No cluster? Play the simulated fallback.

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: agent-egress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      tenant: agent
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: api-allowed
    ports:
    - port: 443

The tenant never held the key.

OpenShell injects the credential on the terminated stream. The agent's environment is clean. The audit log shows the decision.

Live demo: OpenShell, local

$ env | grep -i token
(empty)
$ curl -H "Authorization: placeholder" https://api/
200 OK, upstream authenticated

No cluster? Play the simulated fallback.

version: 1
network_policies:
  agent-net:
    name: agent-network
    endpoints:
      - host: api.allowed.com
        port: 443
        protocol: rest
        enforcement: enforce
        access: read-only
# no matching rule = deny

Fields per OpenShell repo examples. Deny-by-default per security-policy.md.

Treat every agent like a tenant you don't trust yet.

  • Isolate

    gVisor or Kata under every agent, no exceptions

  • Compose

    one CRD, guardrails materialized by the platform

  • Broker

    credentials injected, never handed out

  • Deny

    egress default-deny, allowlist the rest

  • Warm

    make the secure path the fast path
